memory_update.text: NVT should be retained as the reference benchmark for electrical enclosure catalog breadth, UL/NEMA testing, and distributor reach, but not treated as the main underfollowed alpha candidate.
LYTS is the strongest underfollowed direct-fit candidate for retail fixture and display exposure, especially via JSI Store Fixtures and refrigerated display products.
HLMN should be tracked as a second-order inventory-availability and retail merchandising candidate tied to SKU-dense hardware, job-site gear, replenishment, and field service.

Need deeper evidence on backlog, inventory turns, distributor relationships, customer concentration, and end-market mix before any candidate can graduate from Layer 1B to higher-confidence chokepoint status.

A Canadian/OTC microcap lead, Hammond Manufacturing, appeared highly relevant in external context for electrical enclosures and availability-driven distribution, but it was not included because this pass requested US-listed companies and candidate count was capped at four.

summary: Layer 1B underfollowed expansion found one reference enclosure leader and three smaller or less-screened public companies with plausible direct or second-order exposure to retail, commercial buildout, home-improvement, job-site, and warehouse availability components. The strongest direct fits are nVent for electrical enclosures and LSI Industries for retail display fixtures. Hillman is a second-order availability/distribution candidate for SKU-dense retail hardware and job-site consumables. Eastern is a below-USD-300M speculative exception with industrial/security hardware and custom-engineered products that may overlap cabinets, fixtures, locks, latches, and returnable packaging, but needs customer/end-market verification.
